raw_response.overlap_rationale: Both papers are readable full texts published in the same November 2025 issue of International Journal of Research and Innovation in Social Science (Vol. 9, Issue 11; both received 14 November 2025 and accepted 22 November 2025) by the exact same author team (Mwale, Kanyamuna, Moose, and Simui) from James Mwale's PhD thesis at the University of Zambia. They are companion reports ('salami-sliced' articles) analyzing the exact same qualitative fieldwork sample in George Compound, Lusaka, Zambia: N = 29 total participants (10 male and 15 female sanitation programme beneficiaries plus 4 key informants from LCC, ZEMA, NWASCO, LWSC, WDC, and the Water and Sanitation Committee). Both papers share word-for-word identical Background, Methodology, Study Limitations, Suggestions for Future Studies, and Reference sections. Empirically, Study A reports the broader set of institutional, regulatory, infrastructural, and gendered mitigation themes (including KII quotes from ZEMA, LCC, NWASCO, and LWSC alongside beneficiary quotes), whereas Study B extracts and reframes the gendered exclusion/mitigation subset from the exact same interviews—reproducing verbatim the same participant quotes (e.g., GC 6, GC 11, GC 19, and GC 22) and entire Discussion subsections from Study A, while adding one quote on absentee landlords (GC 11). Treating them as independent studies in qualitative or quantitative synthesis would directly double-count the same respondents and verbatim interview excerpts.
raw_response.study_a_sample_and_data: Qualitative interpretive phenomenological study in George Compound (peri-urban Lusaka, Zambia) using criterion-based purposive sampling and reflexive thematic analysis of 50-60 minute in-depth and key informant interviews with N = 29 participants: 25 community beneficiaries (10 males, 15 women, coded GC) who experienced government/Lusaka Sanitation Program interventions over the past 10 years and 4 key informants (coded KII) across the Ward Development Committee, Water and Sanitation Committee, Lusaka City Council (Public Health Department), ZEMA (Inspectorate), NWASCO, and LWSC (Peri-Urban Department).
raw_response.study_b_sample_and_data: Qualitative phenomenological study in George Compound (peri-urban Lusaka, Zambia) using the exact same criterion-based purposive sample and reflexive thematic analysis of 50-60 minute in-depth and key informant interviews with N = 29 participants (10 males, 15 women beneficiaries coded GC, and 4 key informants from WDC, Water and Sanitation Committee, LCC, ZEMA, NWASCO, and LWSC), reporting the gendered exclusion and mitigation subset of findings.
